summary: Arbitrary file write via GeoWebCache FileRasterFilter ZIP update
description:
### Description

The GeoWebCache REST API can update the raster mask of a `FileRasterFilter` by uploading a ZIP file to
`POST /rest/filter/{filterName}/update/zip` (`/gwc/rest/...` in GeoServer).

The grid set id taken from each ZIP entry name was included in the output file path without sanitization or
directory containment check. Combined with the filter `storagePath` and `fileExtension` settings, an administrator
could write files with any content and extension to any directory writable by the GeoWebCache process.

### Impact

An authenticated administrator could write arbitrary files outside the GeoWebCache cache directory, and outside the
GeoServer file system sandbox. On Tomcat, writing a JSP file into a web application directory leads to remote code
execution as the servlet container user.

The attack requires administrator credentials. No `FileRasterFilter` exists by default, but an administrator can
create one through the REST API.

### Mitigation

Run GeoServer / GeoWebCache as a non-root user, with write access limited to the data and cache directories, and
no write access to the servlet container web application directories.

### Resolution

Patched for:
* GeoWebCache 2.0.2 (GeoServer 3.0.2)
* GeoWebCache 1.28.6 (GeoServer 2.28.6)
* GeoWebCache 1.27.6 (GeoServer 2.27.7)

The matrix file is now always written inside the filter `storagePath`, `fileExtension` is limited to raster formats,
and the upload is validated as an image for a configured grid set and zoom level before it is written.

### References

* [#1593](https://github.com/GeoWebCache/geowebcache/pull/1593)

cwes.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory
